pages.description: The best-selling historian sits down with National Geographic to talk about his fast-paced new book that places San Francisco at the center of American events.
pages.text: Nathaniel Philbrick's New Book Could Give You Whiplash | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Nathaniel Philbrick's New Book Could Give You Whiplash The best-selling historian sits down with National Geographic to talk about his fast-paced new book that places San Francisco at the center of American events. A miner's camp on the hillside in El Dorado, California during the gold rush. The history-making event is the subject of a new book by Nathaniel Philbrick. Library of Congress By William O'Connor Published October 6, 2026 However chaotic life may seem, cracking open the latest book from historian Nathaniel Philbrick will make it calm by comparison. The author behind the best-selling In the Heart of the Sea is out with a new work, The Rush: California Gold, the Civil War, and the Making of the Modern World , which chronicles the mad dash to San Francisco in 1849 after gold was accidentally discovered there. The book is action-packed, with page after page of gun-toting politicians, treasonous plots, and unspeakable misery heaped on humans by other humans. Philbrick takes a tale we all think we know enough about— the 49ers —and unravels that tight little story into a series of characters and vignettes that leave one slack-jawed at the topsy-turvy era. All of the tales in the book are in service of a very ambitious goal Philbrick lays out in the title—rethinking the gold rush as more than a merely curious event in American history and instead as one that transformed the country and sent it hurtling toward its fate—the coming civil war. DWGs provide supplemental funding in response to major economic dislocations or other events that cause or contribute to a shortage of existing WIOA Dislocated Worker formula funds and other relevant resources in states and local areas, creating challenges in their ability to provide workforce services to eligible participants. DWGs enable states and communities to respond to and recover from large, often unexpected dislocation events and their associated impacts. The WIOA statute allows the Employment and Training Administration (ETA) to fund two types of DWGs: Disaster Recovery and Employment Recovery. Disaster Recovery DWGs provide funding to create temporary employment opportunities to assist with clean-up and recovery efforts when an area impacted by an emergency or major disaster is declared eligible for public assistance by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) or is declared or recognized as an emergency or disaster of national significance by a Federal agency with authority or jurisdiction over Federal response to the disaster or emergency, including public health emergencies. Unlike national parks, National Heritage Areas are large lived-in landscapes. Consequently, National Heritage Area entities collaborate with communities to determine how to make heritage relevant to local interests and needs. In 1984, the first National Heritage Area, Illinois and Michigan Canal National Heritage Area, was signed into law by President Ronald Reagan. In his dedication speech, Reagan referred to National Heritage Areas as "a new kind of national park" that married heritage conservation, recreation, and economic development. On January 5, 2023, President Biden signed the National Heritage Areas Act (P.L. 117-339) into law. This law established the National Heritage Area System, a statutory framework for the National Park Service’s role in its administration. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn National Historic Oregon Trail Interpretive Center The National Historic Oregon Trail Interpretive Center, located near Baker City, Oregon, brings to life the historic journey of pioneers who traveled westward on the Oregon Trail in the 19th century. This interactive museum and outdoor site illuminates the challenges, triumphs, and profound impact of this historic migration that shaped the American west. Visitors can explore exhibits that showcase the daily lives of the pioneers and the landscapes they traversed. The exhibits also highlight the cultural connections and collisions of the Native Americans and Euro-American emigrants involved in this monumental movement of people. Set on a hillside with stunning views, the center features hands-on exhibits, life-size displays, and a replica wagon camp. The 500-acre site includes remnants of the historic Flagstaff Gold Mine and original ruts carved by pioneer wagons. Through engaging presentations and programs, the Center honors the legacy of the Oregon Trail, providing a fascinating look at the hardships and adventures that defined this pivotal chapter in American history. pages.text: National Veterans' Training Institute | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content National Veterans' Training Institute The U.S. Department of Labor's Veterans' Employment and Training Service (VETS) established the National Veterans' Training Institute (NVTI) in 1986 to provide specialized training and professional skills enhancement of State Workforce Agencies and other veterans' service providers' staff. To perform most effectively, veterans' services professionals require specialized training; and State Workforce Agencies' local job service office and other program management staff need more generalized training. The NVTI strives to meet both needs. The NVTI basic training focuses on improving employment services for veterans through a professional skills-development program. About 70% of participants are Disabled Veterans' Outreach Program specialists and Local Veterans' Employment Representatives; the remaining participants are state employees and administrative staff, federal employees and others involved with veterans' employment and training issues. The NVTI training curriculum is designed to ensure that participants are trained in competencies that meet customers' needs. In addition to the basic employment and training professional-skills course, training is offered in veterans' benefits, case management, marketing and accessing the media, and management of veterans' services. NVTI also offers courses in veterans' reemployment rights case investigation and grants management, to address the training needs of the VETS staff. Management Concepts operates the NVTI

Polynesians were well established on the islands when, about 800 years ago, Polynesians from the Society Islands arrived in Hawai`i. Claiming descent from the greatest gods, they became the new rulers of Hawai`i. After a time of voyaging back and forth between the Society Islands and the Hawaiian Archipelago, contact with southern Polynesia ceased. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. SCIENCE LAELAPS Newfound Fossil Octopus and Squid Were Giants By Riley Black Published March 10, 2015 • 4 min read A good fossil squid is hard to find. The invertebrates are too squishy to leave much behind, and only in truly exceptional circumstances do paleontologists get to see much more than the chitinous supports the cephalopods kept on the inside. Octopus are even more confounding. Without any remnants of an internal shell, the eight-armed quick-change artists are like prehistoric ghosts. But do not despair. The jaws of ancient coleoids give us reason for hope, and have just revealed a pair of prehistoric cephalopods that may have rivaled today’s ocean giants in size. Described by Kazushige Tanabe and colleagues in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , the two lower jaws were found in roughly 80 million year old rock around Hokkaido, Japan’s Haboro-futamata Dam. Both were preserved in three-dimensional detail, providing Tanabe and coworkers with enough anatomical clues to figure out that they were left behind by previously-unknown species. Octopus and squid beaks can be very informative fossils. That’s because marine biologists have spent a great deal of time studying the chitinous beaks of modern cephalopods. Located on the ground floor, the pressroom is supported by the Public Information Office, which is dedicated to facilitating accurate coverage of the Court and furthering the public’s understanding of the Court’s function and history. The main office number is 202-479-3211. Recorded information—such as the opinion and orders forecast for the coming week or the list of opinions released that day—is available on this line, and reporters may also reach a staff member by pressing 1. Close nicofr77's Diary À portée de train : une carte des boucles vélo accessibles en train, depuis 60 villes Posted by nicofr77 on 2 October 2026 in French (Français) . Last updated on 4 October 2026. Je publie sur Tisseur de Voies, le site où je calcule des boucles vélo avec retour en train, une carte qui répond à une question simple : depuis ma ville, jusqu’où puis-je partir à vélo en prenant un seul train ? On choisit une ville parmi 60 et une durée de train aller, de 0 à 4 heures. La carte montre en rose les véloroutes des boucles qu’on peut rejoindre, et en bleu les gares atteintes, plus foncées quand elles sont proches. Ici, Paris avec une heure de train : 1 763 boucles, contre 323 qui partent des gares parisiennes. Une boucle, c’est un itinéraire à vélo d’une gare à une autre sur des véloroutes balisées, avec un train pour rentrer. Elle compte dès qu’un train aller atteint l’une de ses gares dans la durée choisie. Un classement des 60 villes accompagne la carte : Paris, Strasbourg et Lille en tête, Brest et Quimper en queue. Les véloroutes viennent d’OpenStreetMap et du référentiel national des véloroutes, le fond de carte d’OpenStreetMap. Les durées sortent des horaires publiés en open data par la SNCF, Île-de-France Mobilités, la Région Sud et les Chemins de fer de la Corse : pour chaque trajet, la durée médiane de la ligne la plus rapide qui circule au moins une fois par jour. Seuls les trains sans changement comptent.

pages.text: Nike faces religious ban in Libya because it was named after Greek goddess Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes 3 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basma El Atti AFP via Getty Images Nike clothes are popular in Libya, although many are counterfeit Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo. The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings. It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god. Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name. The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country. It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/bioscience/nist-bioeconomy-lexicon Biotechnology NIST Bioeconomy Lexicon Summary Biotechnology and biomanufacturing are increasingly vital to the global economy, including in the health care, food and agriculture, and energy sectors. Accordingly, there is a need for standardized terms and definitions to ensure a common understanding of the concepts, data, technical developments, and workforce opportunities as the bioeconomy grows both domestically and internationally. The list of terms and definition related to bioeconomy was developed by NIST in consultation with an interagency working group consisting of several U.S. government departments and agencies, and reflects consideration of relevant domestic and international definitions as well as those from private sector stakeholders. The lexicon harmonizes a base set of terms and definitions with the goal of helping to enable the development of measurements and measurement methods for the bioeconomy that support uses such as economic measurement, risk assessments, and the application of machine learning and other artificial intelligence tools.
